name: Chin wing osteotomy

lead: A chin wing osteotomy is an oral and maxillofacial surgery technique that extends a sliding genioplasty back along the lower border of the jaw. The cut bone is repositioned and the gaps are typically filled with bone graft, which can advance and lengthen the chin and add width and definition toward the jaw angle.

Surgeons describe it for retrognathic chins, jaw asymmetry and lower-face contour, sometimes together with orthognathic surgery. Published evidence consists mainly of technical notes and small case series.

paras: It is done by a surgeon under general anaesthesia, often planned with digital imaging and sometimes with custom cutting guides and plates. Some patients compare it with custom jaw-angle implants, a choice discussed at length on looksmaxxing forums.

A 2026 study notes the main concern is inferior alveolar nerve damage, which makes the procedure less used than classic genioplasty. Forum users report dissatisfaction, contour problems and revisions in some cases. Surgeon experience matters.

angle.text: Patients use it to reshape the chin and lower jaw outline with their own bone rather than an implant. It can advance and widen the lower third.

lead: Chin wing osteotomy is an extended form of genioplasty in which the cut runs from the chin region along the body of the mandible toward the jaw angle, allowing the lower border to be moved forward or reshaped. Albino Triaca's 'chin wing' technique is the one commonly cited. [1][2]

People seek it to project a recessed chin, lengthen the lower third, and add width at the gonial angle while leaving bite alignment alone. Case reports describe patients with normal occlusion treated for retrognathic mandible with virtual planning and cutting guides. [3]

The literature is largely technical notes and case reports, plus a small retrospective series on nerve outcomes. On looksmax.org it is discussed as 'genioplasty on steroids' and compared with custom implants, with both enthusiasts and users who report regrets. [4][5]

paras: A mini wing variant ends the posterior cut at the mandibular notch's upper part, leaves the lower border intact, and can be combined with bilateral sagittal split osteotomy. Its authors say a low inferior alveolar nerve is not a contraindication for it, unlike the traditional wing. [6]

A 2021 technical note described custom guides and implants intended to make the procedure safer and quicker, and a 2021 case report combined a chin wing with a bone-graft pyramid and malar implants. [7][8]

Genioplasty in general is performed mainly for cosmetic profile and facial balance reasons. [9] Reported uses of the wing variant include asymmetric mandibles such as Goldenhar syndrome and condylar hyperplasia, hyperdivergent skeletal class III deformity, and cosmetic contour in people with normal occlusion. [3][1][10]
A 2026 retrospective study of 26 patients examined nerve damage because the greater inferior alveolar nerve risk is why the technique is used less than classic genioplasty. [11]
Forum threads weigh chin wing against custom jaw-angle implants, with some posters asking why it draws negative comments and others reporting disappointment or revisions. [4][5]
Published human reports are technical notes and small case series, including two retrognathic patients followed four years after planned surgery and a 26-patient nerve study. [11][3][6]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the procedure is debated against custom implants and conventional genioplasty. [4]
